title: gDNA Extraction with QuickExtract
author: Eric Danner
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7kyhkxw
materials: To extract the gDNA from the cells: Put on thermocyclcer 65C for 15 min 68C for 15 min 98C for 10 min Hold at 4C *I have left at 4C for months and things work fine. Also I have frozen and thawed and it works fine.

steps.title: Calculate required cell number
steps.instruction: Determine the number of diploid human cells needed for the desired gDNA amount using the conversion 1 cell ≈ 6 pg gDNA (2N). For example, 100 ng gDNA ≈ 16,000 cells (32,000 alleles). To obtain 100 µl of 50 ng/µl gDNA, resuspend 8,000,000 cells in 100 µl QuickExtract.

steps.title: Count cells and pellet
steps.instruction: Count cells, then transfer the calculated amount into a 96‑well plate and centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 2 min to pellet the cells.

steps.title: Wash cell pellet (optional)
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet once with PBS (or simply tap dry). If a wash was performed, centrifuge again to re‑pellet the cells.

steps.title: Resuspend in QuickExtract
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in QuickExtract solution (typically 20–50 µl for quick genotyping; use 100 µl when following the 8,000,000‑cell calculation).

steps.title: Mix and transfer
steps.instruction: Pipette the suspension up and down to mix thoroughly, then transfer the lysate to a PCR strip tube.

steps.title: PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Set up PCR using PrimeStar GXL polymerase and run 35 cycles (standard quick‑genotyping conditions).
